title: Safety Fence Orchestrator and Soft Lending — PRD sketch
summary: Draft proposal for a Safety Fence Orchestrator (SFO): a lightweight runtime and policy layer that enables controlled cross-tenant soft lending of reserved capacity, enforcement of fidelity gates (degraded compute profiles), and an eviction-resistant isolation fence. Goal is to reduce customer-visible outages during transient demand spikes while preserving isolation guarantees and clear economics.
problem_statement: Dedicated pools frequently see short, high-intensity spikes from one or a few tenants that: (a) exhaust headroom and cause latency SLO violations for other tenants; (b) force aggressive evictions or hard throttles that are disruptive to customers; (c) lead to manual ops triage and poor utilization. Current options (hard preemption, fixed burst credits, or naive autoscaling) either erode isolation, increase cost, or miss short spikes.
goals: 1) Reduce tail SLO breaches caused by transient blasts without increasing hard-evictions. 2) Recover more user work in place by offering controlled temporary capacity loans. 3) Provide transparent controls and billing for borrowed capacity. 4) Offer staged fidelity options (compute degradation) as a first fallback before capacity loans/evictions. 5) Make behavior observable and reversible.
non_goals: 1) Replace long-term capacity planning or committed reservations. 2) Offer unmetered unlimited bursting. 3) Remove tenant-level SLA guarantees by default.
requirements: - Runtime-level low-latency decisioning (<100ms) for accepting/denying a loan. - Policy expressions per-tenant (max loan %, loan TTL, allowed fidelity levels). - Audit trail for loan events and fidelity switches. - Console controls: ability to opt-in/out, set repayment rules, and view loan ledger. - Billing events surfaced to invoice system and cost buckets. - Graceful fallback stack: fidelity gates -> soft loan -> soft-throttle -> eviction.
proposed_design_overview: SFO comprises three cooperating subsystems: (A) Policy engine (declarative tenant policies and global pool rules); (B) Loan broker (real-time loan matching, ledger, TTL enforcement); (C) Fidelity controller (runtime knobs to accept lower-fidelity execution: shorter KV cache, quantized model variants, lower concurrency). A centralized controller exposes APIs and a local per-host agent enforces transient decisions to meet latency targets.
runtime_flow: 1) Incoming request evaluated against routing and tenant SLO budget. 2) If capacity pressure detected, evaluate fidelity gate for the tenant (if configured) — if enabled, attempt degrade path. 3) If fidelity not allowed or insufficient, request loan from Loan Broker. 4) Broker applies policy, checks escrow balance and global headroom, and issues a loan token with TTL and repayment terms. 5) Local agent accepts token and provisions ephemeral slot or soft weight. 6) Telemetry emitted for every step. 7) On TTL expiry, repayment path triggered: borrower reduces usage, or repayment credit consumed against next invoice, or debt triggers scheduled soft-throttle.
policy_model: - Tenant policy attributes: max_loan_percent (string percentage), repayment_mode (string: invoice_credit|priority_decay|rate_limit), loan_ttl_seconds (string), allowed_fidelity_levels (list of strings). - Global rules: pool_max_concurrent_loans, pool_loan_cap_percent, emergency_disable_flag.
api_contracts_examples: - POST /v1/dedicated/loans/request {tenant_id, requested_rps, justification, preferred_fidelity} -> {approved: true|false, token, ttl, terms}. - GET /v1/dedicated/loans/ledger?tenant_id= -> list of ledger entries. - POST /v1/dedicated/fidelity/apply {tenant_id, fidelity_level} -> ack. - Admin: POST /v1/admin/loans/adjust {tenant_id, delta_percent}.
console_and_ux: - Tenant page: toggle Safety Fence opt-in, set repayment preference, view active loans and history. - Pool page: heatmap of outstanding loan % by tenant, loan ledger, current headroom. - Alerting: loan-consumption > X% for Y minutes, loan-default events. - Rollout knobs: global switch, per-pool pilot, canary to small set of tenants.
observability_and_metrics: Primary metrics to track: loan_approved_rate, loan_rejected_rate, loan_ttl_expiry_count, loan_repayment_success_rate, p99_latency_by_tenancy_during-loans, eviction_count_during-loans, fidelity_fallback_rate, percentage_of_tokens_served_under_degraded_fidelity. Add tracing spans for broker decision path.
operational_playbook_notes: - If pool loan saturation > pool_loan_cap_percent: start rejecting non-critical loans and notify SRE. - If repayment defaults > 5% for 1 hour: escalate to billing and customer-success. - Emergency disable: global emergency_disable_flag immediate hard disable of loans and roll back to preconfigured soft-throttle. - Simulation harness: extend existing dedicated-sim with synthetic tenant blasts to validate behavior prior to rollout.
billing_and_economics: - Loans are tracked as 'borrowed compute' line items; default repayment is invoice_credit with explicit rate per loaned-second or loaned-vGPU-equivalent. - Alternative: allow repayment via priority_decay where future burst priority is reduced proportionally. - Need pricing model + cost simulation for typical customer patterns.
safety_and_isolation_guarantees: - Maximum aggregate loan exposure per pool is capped. - Loans cannot be used to circumvent data locality/isolation constraints; loan tokens are only valid within same pool/region. - Fidelity degradations must preserve tenant data isolation and not enable cross-tenant caching leaks.
risk_and_mitigation: - Risk: misconfigured policies could let a noisy tenant borrow and starve others. Mitigation: default conservative caps, strong console defaults, and a canary windows. - Risk: complexity of billing confusion — mitigation: clear ledger entries, automatic invoice line items and CS playbook. - Risk: runtime latency overhead of loan checks — mitigation: local caching of broker decisions for TTL period and minimal decision payloads.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulations + offline cost model (2 weeks). Phase 1: Internal Canary on non-critical pool + ops runbook (4 weeks). Phase 2: Invite handful of pilot customers with opt-in + billing preview (6–8 weeks). Phase 3: Gradual enablement with conservative defaults + automated rollback triggers (4 weeks). Phase 4: GA with full billing and advanced policies.
success_metrics: - Reduce cross-tenant eviction incidents by 40% in pilot pools. - Reduce latency SLO breaches attributable to transient spikes by 30%. - Loan repayment disputes under 2% in first 90 days. - Pilot customer satisfaction (qual) >= neutral-positive.
open_questions: - What is the canonical mapping between loan units and billing units (tokens vs vGPU-seconds)? - Should loans be transferable across pools within an org? (security/isolation tradeoff) - How do we represent partial fidelity fallbacks in metrics and cost? - How to simulate adversarial tenants that try to game loan TTLs? - Do we expose an SLA for loan availability or are loans best-effort?
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike: build Broker prototype + local-agent hook (owner: Marco). 2) Sim team: extend dedicated-sim workload generator for loan scenarios (owner: Lena). 3) Product: refine repayment price model and billing events (owner: Priya). 4) Security review for cross-pool tokens (owner: Omar). 5) Draft API + console mockups and review with Solutions Eng (owner: Sofia).
notes_to_self: Keep the first pilot extremely conservative: max_loan_percent=10, pool_loan_cap_percent=8, loan_ttl_seconds=60. Focus on observability and clear invoice artifacts — billing confusion is the quickest path to unhappy customers.
